intents.assessment_focus: Recognize which AI subfield or technique a given real-world scenario exemplifies.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize which single AI subfield a described real-world scenario exemplifies.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should name a plausible but incorrect AI subfield that superficially resembles the scenario, e.g. confusing search-based pathfinding with machine learning.
generation_constraints: Use an introductory recognition task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Identify appropriate applications of AI in different fields.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not present a scenario that plausibly fits more than one subfield equally well.
Do not require ranking or comparing multiple scenarios.
prohibited_conflations: conflating machine learning with AI in general
conflating a specific technique such as search with any AI application whatsoever
intents.question_archetype: AI subfield recognition from a real-world scenario
required_concepts: AI subfields (search, machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision)
mapping a concrete real-world scenario to the technique it exemplifies
required_question_characteristics: State one clear real-world scenario.
Ask which single AI subfield or technique the scenario exemplifies.

intents.assessment_focus: Recognize whether a described problem is well-suited to an AI-based approach or is better solved with a simple deterministic procedure.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize whether a described task calls for AI techniques or a straightforward fixed procedure.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should mislabel a simple, fully-specified arithmetic or lookup task as requiring AI.
generation_constraints: Use an introductory recognition task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Identify appropriate applications of AI in different fields.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not describe a task that plausibly could go either way.
Do not require naming a specific AI subfield in this intent.
prohibited_conflations: any computational task automatically counts as an AI application
required_concepts: tasks suited to AI (pattern recognition, ambiguous or complex mapping, large search space)
tasks better solved by a simple fixed procedure
required_question_characteristics: Describe one concrete problem or task.
Ask whether it is well-suited to an AI-based approach or better solved with a simple deterministic procedure.

intents.assessment_focus: Given a named AI subfield, identify which of two candidate real-world scenario descriptions is an example of it.
intents.cognitive_demand: Given a named AI subfield, identify which of two candidate scenarios exemplifies it.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should pick the scenario that superficially resembles the subfield's name without matching its actual technique.
generation_constraints: Use an introductory recognition task.
Provide exactly one defensible answer supported by the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Identify appropriate applications of AI in different fields.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not describe two scenarios that both plausibly exemplify the named subfield.
prohibited_conflations: any application involving a computer program counts as an example of the named subfield
required_concepts: named AI subfield definition
matching an application example to its subfield
required_question_characteristics: Name one AI subfield and describe two candidate real-world scenarios.
Ask which scenario is an example of the named subfield.

intents.assessment_focus: Compare two candidate AI approaches for solving a described problem and judge which is the better fit.
intents.cognitive_demand: Compare a search-based approach against a learning-based approach to judge which better fits a described problem.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should pick the approach that does not match the problem's structure (e.g. search for a problem needing pattern generalization from data).
generation_constraints: Use an intermediate comparison task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Identify appropriate applications of AI in different fields.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not describe a problem where both approaches are equally appropriate.
prohibited_conflations: a search-based approach and a learning-based approach are interchangeable for any AI problem
required_concepts: search-based approach
learning-based approach
problem-approach fit
required_question_characteristics: Describe one problem and two candidate approaches (e.g. a search-based approach and a learning-based approach).
Ask which candidate approach is the better fit and why.

intents.assessment_focus: Diagnose why a stated classification of a real-world AI application into a named subfield is incorrect.
intents.cognitive_demand: Diagnose why a described application has been mislabeled with the wrong AI subfield.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should defend the incorrect label using a surface-level resemblance to the named subfield.
generation_constraints: Use an intermediate diagnostic task.
Provide exactly one defensible answer supported by the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Identify appropriate applications of AI in different fields.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not assert a subfield label that is actually correct.
prohibited_conflations: a superficial resemblance between two applications means they use the same AI subfield
required_concepts: subfield misclassification
distinguishing surface similarity from underlying technique
required_question_characteristics: Describe a real-world AI application together with an asserted, incorrect subfield label for it.
Ask why that label is incorrect.

intents.assessment_focus: Apply a stated practical constraint, such as limited labeled data or a need for explainable decisions, to judge which of two candidate AI approaches is more appropriate.
intents.cognitive_demand: Apply a stated data-availability or explainability constraint to judge which candidate AI approach is more appropriate.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should recommend the approach the constraint actually rules out.
generation_constraints: Use an intermediate application task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Identify appropriate applications of AI in different fields.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not state a constraint that both candidate approaches satisfy equally well.
prohibited_conflations: the most powerful AI approach is always the appropriate choice regardless of practical constraints
required_concepts: data availability as a constraint on approach choice
explainability as a constraint on approach choice
required_question_characteristics: State one practical constraint (e.g. very little labeled data available, or a need for explainable decisions) and two candidate approaches.
Ask which approach the constraint favors.

intents.assessment_focus: Given a description of the Turing Test or the Chinese Room argument, identify what it claims to test or argue.
intents.cognitive_demand: Given a description of the Turing Test or the Chinese Room argument, identify what it claims to test or argue.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should swap the Turing Test's behavioral claim with the Chinese Room's understanding-based challenge, or vice versa.
generation_constraints: Use an introductory recognition task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
Use the exact framing "test or argue", not "test or demonstrate" -- per the approved amendment to AI-FND-04-INT-02.
intents.learning_objective: Explain how the Turing Test and Chinese Room argument relate to machine intelligence and understanding.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not require the learner to judge whether the argument succeeds.
Do not blend both the Turing Test and the Chinese Room into one single description.
prohibited_conflations: conflating what the Turing Test measures (behavioral indistinguishability in conversation) with what the Chinese Room challenges (genuine understanding)
treating the Chinese Room as itself a test for detecting a machine, rather than an argument against the sufficiency of the Turing Test
intents.question_archetype: Turing Test vs. Chinese Room claim recognition
required_concepts: the Turing Test as a behavioral test conducted through conversation
the Chinese Room argument as a challenge to whether behavior alone establishes understanding
required_question_characteristics: Describe either the Turing Test or the Chinese Room argument.
Ask what that description claims to test or argue about machine intelligence or understanding.

intents.assessment_focus: Recognize how the Turing Test is conducted, in terms of the interrogator, the person, and the machine.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize the roles of the interrogator, the person, and the machine in how the Turing Test is conducted.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should claim the interrogator can see or directly examine the machine rather than only converse with it.
generation_constraints: Use an introductory recognition task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Explain how the Turing Test and Chinese Room argument relate to machine intelligence and understanding.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not require judging a specific transcript in this intent.
prohibited_conflations: the interrogator directly observes which participant is the machine rather than only conversing with them
required_concepts: interrogator separated from the person and the machine
the interrogator's goal of determining which is which
required_question_characteristics: Describe the setup of the interrogator, the person, and the machine.
Ask what the interrogator's task is in this setup.

intents.assessment_focus: Recognize what the Chinese Room argument's setup involves and what it claims about a system that manipulates symbols according to a program.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize the Chinese Room's setup and its claim that following a program does not by itself grant understanding.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should claim the man (or the computer) understands Chinese because the program produces correct responses.
generation_constraints: Use an introductory recognition task.
Provide exactly one defensible answer supported by the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Explain how the Turing Test and Chinese Room argument relate to machine intelligence and understanding.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not require the learner to judge whether the argument succeeds in this intent.
prohibited_conflations: the man in the room understands Chinese as long as he correctly follows the program's instructions
required_concepts: the man in the room implementing a program for manipulating symbols
the argument's claim that program-following alone does not entail understanding
required_question_characteristics: Describe the man in the room following a program to manipulate symbols.
Ask what the argument claims about whether he, or any computer doing the same, understands Chinese.

intents.assessment_focus: Apply the Turing Test's setup to judge whether a described interrogator/machine exchange would count as the machine passing the test.
intents.cognitive_demand: Apply the behavioral-indistinguishability criterion to judge whether a described exchange counts as passing the Turing Test.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should judge the machine by factual accuracy rather than by indistinguishability from the person.
generation_constraints: Use an intermediate diagnostic task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Explain how the Turing Test and Chinese Room argument relate to machine intelligence and understanding.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not describe an exchange where the interrogator's ability to distinguish them is ambiguous.
prohibited_conflations: the Turing Test is passed by the machine giving factually correct answers rather than by being indistinguishable from the person
required_concepts: interrogator's inability to reliably distinguish machine from person
passing the Turing Test as a behavioral outcome
required_question_characteristics: Describe a conversation between the interrogator and the machine, and whether the interrogator could reliably tell it was the machine.
Ask whether the machine passed the Turing Test.

intents.assessment_focus: Diagnose a described restatement of the Chinese Room argument that misrepresents what the argument actually claims.
intents.cognitive_demand: Diagnose why a described restatement of the Chinese Room argument misrepresents its actual, narrower claim.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should accept the overreaching restatement as an accurate summary of the argument.
generation_constraints: Use an intermediate diagnostic task.
Provide exactly one defensible answer supported by the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Explain how the Turing Test and Chinese Room argument relate to machine intelligence and understanding.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not present a restatement that is actually an accurate paraphrase.
prohibited_conflations: the Chinese Room argument claims computers can never behave as if they understand, rather than that behavior alone does not establish genuine understanding
required_concepts: the argument's narrow target: program-following alone does not entail understanding
common misreadings of the argument
required_question_characteristics: State a described restatement of the Chinese Room argument that overreaches its actual claim.
Ask what is wrong with that restatement.

intents.assessment_focus: Compare what the Turing Test and the Chinese Room argument each do and do not establish about machine intelligence or understanding.
intents.cognitive_demand: Compare the behavioral claim of the Turing Test against the understanding-based challenge of the Chinese Room.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should claim the two establish the same conclusion about machine understanding.
generation_constraints: Use an intermediate comparison task.
Keep every factual claim within the mapped reference passages.
intents.learning_objective: Explain how the Turing Test and Chinese Room argument relate to machine intelligence and understanding.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not ask which argument is correct; ask only what each one claims or implies.
prohibited_conflations: passing the Turing Test and satisfying the Chinese Room's understanding standard are the same achievement
required_concepts: Turing Test as evidence of behavioral capability, not proof of understanding
Chinese Room as a challenge to inferring understanding from behavior alone
required_question_characteristics: Describe both the Turing Test and the Chinese Room argument together.
Ask what each one does, and does not, establish about machine intelligence or understanding.
